# pangolin_health_check (Resource)

Manages a standalone Pangolin health check: a probe run by a site's Newt connector that is not attached to any target. Its health can drive alert rules.

> **Note:** Requires Pangolin Enterprise Edition (written against 1.24.0). The routes do not exist on the OSS build, which answers 404.

> **Note:** Newt silently skips a probe that has no `hostname` or `port`, and an `http` probe that has no `path`. The server only enforces `hostname` when `enabled = true`.

> **Note:** the API cannot clear `port` once set. Removing it from the configuration keeps the last value. Removing `hostname`, `path`, `scheme`, `tls_server_name`, `status` or `headers` clears them on the server.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# HTTP probe run by the homelab site's Newt connector.
resource "pangolin_health_check" "api" {
  name    = "api"
  site_id = pangolin_site.homelab.id
  enabled = true

  mode     = "http"
  scheme   = "https"
  hostname = "api.internal"
  port     = 8443
  path     = "/healthz"
  method   = "GET"
  status   = 200

  interval            = 30
  unhealthy_interval  = 10
  timeout             = 5
  healthy_threshold   = 2
  unhealthy_threshold = 3

  headers = [
    { name = "X-Probe", value = "pangolin" },
  ]
}

# Plain TCP connect check.
resource "pangolin_health_check" "postgres" {
  name     = "postgres"
  site_id  = pangolin_site.homelab.id
  enabled  = true
  mode     = "tcp"
  hostname = "db.internal"
  port     = 5432
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name of the health check.
- `site_id` (Number) The ID of the site whose Newt connector runs the probe. Changing it recreates the health check: an in-place site change on Pangolin 1.24 pushes the probe to the new site but leaves it running on the old one.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the probe runs. Defaults to `false`, like the API.
- `follow_redirects` (Boolean) Whether an `http` probe follows redirects. Defaults to `true`.
- `headers` (Attributes List) Request headers set on an `http` probe - list of `{name, value}` objects. Leave unset (or `[]`) for no probe headers. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--headers))
- `healthy_threshold` (Number) Consecutive successful probes required to mark the check healthy. Defaults to `1`.
- `hostname` (String) Host the probe connects to. Required when `enabled = true`.
- `interval` (Number) Probe interval in seconds while the check is healthy. Defaults to `30`.
- `method` (String) HTTP method used by an `http` probe (e.g. `GET`, `HEAD`). Defaults to `GET`.
- `mode` (String) Probe mode: `http` or `tcp`. Defaults to `http`.
- `path` (String) URL path requested by an `http` probe (e.g. `/health`).
- `port` (Number) Port the probe connects to.
- `scheme` (String) Scheme used by an `http` probe (`http` or `https`).
- `status` (Number) Expected HTTP status code of an `http` probe (e.g. `200`).
- `timeout` (Number) Probe timeout in seconds. Defaults to `5`, the Pangolin UI and database default (the API alone would store `1`).
- `tls_server_name` (String) TLS SNI used when an `http` probe uses `https`.
- `unhealthy_interval` (Number) Probe interval in seconds while the check is unhealthy. Defaults to `30`.
- `unhealthy_threshold` (Number) Consecutive failed probes required to mark the check unhealthy. Defaults to `1`.

### Read-Only

- `health` (String) Current health as reported by Pangolin (`unknown`, `healthy`, `unhealthy`).
- `id` (Number) The numeric health check ID.

<a id="nestedatt--headers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `headers`

Required:

- `name` (String) Header name.
- `value` (String) Header value.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Standalone health checks import by numeric ID. Look it up via the
# pangolin_health_checks data source.
terraform import pangolin_health_check.example <health_check_id>
```
